Law no. 33/2022 "On open data and reuse of public sector information" in Article 6 "Definitions", point 11 provides that:
"Reuse" is the use by natural or legal persons of documents held by public sector bodies within the framework of public duty or public enterprises within the framework of the services they provide, for commercial or non-commercial purposes, other than the original purpose to which document was produced.

column4:
Open Data impact: Enabling increased data accessibility opens doors for expanding research through the utilization and generation of new insights from openly available data. It amplifies the prominence of one's research endeavors. By actively sharing and promptly analyzing data, productivity is heightened, and more efficient workflows are established. This accessibility empowers any individual to replicate and validate experiments. It elevates researcher accountability while curbing instances of academic dishonesty. Furthermore, it streamlines interdisciplinary research efforts, nurturing partnerships among scholars. Optimal data reutilization is achieved by opting for formats that facilitate effective data extraction.

Article 19 of Law no. 33/2022 "On open data and the reuse of public sector information" provides that "The Commissioner for the Right to Information and Protection of Personal Data is the body responsible for the protection, supervision and promotion of the right to reuse documents according to this the law".
During 2014, the Commissioner has started written communication with public sector bodies and public enterprises in RSH to make them aware of the implementation of the law on open data. During this process, it has assisted these institutions for any ambiguity and is monitoring the implementation of this law by OSP and SP.
